event_date_basis: The official OpenAI RSS feed (https://openai.com/news/rss.xml, fetched directly, HTTP 200, 1,194 items, newest 2026-09-16) carries the item 'Accelerating the next phase of AI' with pubDate 'Tue, 31 Mar 2026 13:00:00 GMT' and guid/link https://openai.com/index/accelerating-the-next-phase-ai. The article page itself carries the byline 'March 31, 2026' and opens 'Today, we closed our latest funding round'. So the announcement date and the round's close date are the same day: 2026-03-31. They are NOT the same as the money-in dates: SoftBank's own filings show its first USD 10.0bn tranche executed 2026-04-01, the second 2026-07-01 and a third planned for 2026-10-01. OpenAI's own sitemap gives the page a lastmod of 2026-08-13T23:42:20.362Z, but a body-text diff of the 2026-04-05 and 2026-09-15 archive captures shows the article text is byte-identical - the lastmod is a site-template rebuild, not a content revision. news_date and slug date = 2026-03-31.
sourcing_notes: READ THIS FIRST - how the main source was reached. openai.com/index/* returns HTTP 403 to every client in this container (confirmed again today: /index/accelerating-the-next-phase-ai, with and without trailing slash, plus /index/.../index.txt and /news/ all 403). The full body of OpenAI's announcement was therefore read from two Internet Archive captures of that exact official URL: 20260915092422 (385,817 bytes) and 20260405075032 (321,567 bytes). This is an archive of OpenAI's own page, not a news report. Three independent checks confirm the capture is authentic and unrevised: (1) the capture's og:description is verbatim identical to the description in OpenAI's own RSS feed, which I fetched directly from openai.com; (2) the capture's byline 'March 31, 2026' matches the feed's official pubDate; (3) a diff of the April and September captures shows the 26 body paragraphs are identical - only navigation chrome differs. IN THE CONTENT PACK, CITE THE CANONICAL URL https://openai.com/index/accelerating-the-next-phase-ai/ , NOT THE ARCHIVE URL. That canonical URL is not a guess: it appears as the guid and link in OpenAI's own RSS feed, and as a <loc> with hreflang alternates in OpenAI's own sitemap at https://openai.com/sitemap.xml/company/ (HTTP 200, 261 entries, fetched directly from openai.com today). WHAT I REACHED DIRECTLY, NO ARCHIVE: openai.com/news/rss.xml (200); openai.com/sitemap.xml and openai.com/sitemap.xml/company/ (200 - a useful first-party way to confirm a canonical /index/ URL and its lastmod without ever guessing); openai.com/robots.txt (200); group.softbank/en/news/press/20260227, /20260327, /20260401_0, /20260701 (all 200, full text rendered to curl); press.aboutamazon.com/2026/2/openai-and-amazon-announce-strategic-partnership (200) and www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/amazon-open-ai-strategic-partnership-investment (200). WHAT I COULD NOT REACH: every openai.com/index/* page including the official zh-Hant translation at openai.com/zh-Hant/index/accelerating-the-next-phase-ai/ (403); openai.com/news/ listing (403); web.archive.org's CDX search API (503, 'Internet Archive services are temporarily offline' - the availability API and the direct /web/<timestamp>/ snapshot URLs still worked); ir.aboutamazon.com RSS (403, Cloudflare); group.softbank RSS paths (404, no feed). NO NVIDIA FIRST-PARTY PAGE about this round was found: nvidianews.nvidia.com/releases.xml is live (20 items, newest 2026-09-16) but only goes back to 2026-08-31, and a domain-restricted search of nvidianews/blogs.nvidia/investor.nvidia surfaced only the September 2025 10-gigawatt partnership, not a March 2026 release. NO ARK INVEST first-party page confirming the ETF inclusion was found on ark-funds.com / ark-invest.com. VERDICT: full. The complete official announcement text is in hand and cross-validated two ways from openai.com itself, and two further first-party corroborating sources (SoftBank Group IR, Amazon press centre) were fetched directly with no archive involved. If the house rule is that an archive read may never back a recorded fact, then downgrade to 'partial': the SoftBank, Amazon, feed and sitemap material alone still supports a solid short article, but the user-facing numbers (900M weekly users, 50M subscribers, the superapp plan) would all have to be dropped.

verified_facts.fact: The page's own byline reads 'March 31, 2026' and it is filed under the category 'Company'. The headline on the page is 'OpenAI raises $122 billion to accelerate the next phase of AI' (the feed title is the shorter 'Accelerating the next phase of AI').
verified_facts.verbatim_quote:
OpenAI
March 31, 2026
Company
OpenAI raises $122 billion to accelerate the next phase of AI

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says it closed the round on the day of the announcement with $122 billion in committed capital at a post-money valuation of $852 billion. Note the wording is 'committed capital', not cash received.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Today, we closed our latest funding round with $122 billion in committed capital at a post money valuation of $852 billion.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says ChatGPT had more than 900 million weekly active users and over 50 million subscribers at the time of the announcement.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: ChatGPT is the overwhelming leader in consumer AI with more than 900 million weekly active users, and over 50 million subscribers.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says it was the fastest technology platform to reach 10 million users and 100 million users, and will 'soon' be the fastest to 1 billion weekly active users. It gives no date for the 1 billion milestone.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: OpenAI was the fastest technology platform to reach 10 million users, the fastest to 100 million users, and soon the fastest to 1 billion weekly active users.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says it is now generating $2B in revenue per month; that it reached $1B in revenue within a year of launching ChatGPT; and that by the end of 2024 it was generating $1B per quarter. It also claims it is growing revenue four times faster than Alphabet and Meta did.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Within a year of launching ChatGPT, we reached $1B in revenue. By the end of 2024 we were generating $1B per quarter. We are now generating $2B in revenue per month.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says the round was anchored by Amazon, NVIDIA and SoftBank, with continued participation from Microsoft; and that SoftBank co-led alongside a16z, D. E. Shaw Ventures, MGX, TPG, and accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc. OpenAI gives NO per-investor amounts anywhere in the post.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: The round was anchored by our strategic partners Amazon, NVIDIA, and SoftBank, with continued participation from our long-term partner, Microsoft. SoftBank co-led the round alongside a16z, D. E. Shaw Ventures, MGX, TPG, and accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI lists the other participating institutions as Altimeter, Appaloosa LP, ARK Invest, affiliated funds of BlackRock, Blackstone, Coatue, D1 Capital Partners, Dragoneer, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Goanna Capital, Insight Partners, The Paragon Group, Sands Capital, Sequoia Capital, Sound Ventures, Temasek, Thrive Capital, UC Investments (University of California CIO Office), and Winslow Capital.

OpenAI says that for the first time it extended participation to investors through bank channels, raising over $3 billion from individual investors. It does not name a single bank or channel, and does not say which countries this was open to.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: For the first time, we extended participation to investors through bank channels, raising over $3 billion from individual investors.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says it is also announcing that OpenAI will be included in several exchange-traded funds managed by ARK Invest. It does not name the funds, give tickers, or give a date.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Today, we're also announcing that OpenAI will be included in several exchange-traded funds managed by ARK Invest, further broadening ownership and giving more people the opportunity to share in the upside economics of OpenAI and the AI era.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says it expanded its existing revolving credit facility to approximately $4.7 billion, supported by a syndicate of JPMorgan Chase, Citi, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo, Mizuho, Royal Bank of Canada, SMBC, UBS, HSBC and Santander, and that the facility remained undrawn at close.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: We have also expanded our existing revolving credit facility to approximately $4.7 billion ... The facility remains undrawn at close.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says enterprise now makes up more than 40% of its revenue and is on track to reach parity with consumer by the end of 2026.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Momentum is just as strong on the enterprise side, which now makes up more than 40% of our revenue, and is on track to reach parity with consumer by the end of 2026.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says its APIs now process more than 15 billion tokens per minute, and that Codex serves over 2 million weekly users, up 5x in the past three months, with usage growing more than 70% month over month.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Our APIs now process more than 15 billion tokens per minute. Codex now serves over 2 million weekly users, up 5x in the past three months, with usage growing more than 70% month over month.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says ChatGPT has 6x the monthly web visits and mobile sessions of the next largest AI app, that total AI time spent is 4x the next largest AI app and 4x all others combined, that search usage has nearly tripled in a year, and that its ads pilot reached more than $100 million in ARR in under six weeks. OpenAI names no measurement source for any of these comparisons.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: ChatGPT has 6x the monthly web visits and mobile sessions than the next largest AI app, while total AI time spent is 4x the next largest AI app and 4x all others combined. Search usage has nearly tripled in a year, and our ads pilot reached more than $100 million in ARR in under six weeks.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says it is building a unified AI superapp that will bring together ChatGPT, Codex, browsing and its broader agentic capabilities into one agent-first experience. No launch date, product name, price, plan tier or region is given, and it does not say what happens to the existing separate apps.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Our superapp will bring together ChatGPT, Codex, browsing, and our broader agentic capabilities into one agent-first experience.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI describes its infrastructure portfolio as spanning cloud through Microsoft, Oracle, AWS, CoreWeave and Google Cloud; silicon through NVIDIA, AMD, AWS Trainium, Cerebras and its own chip in partnership with Broadcom; and data centres through partnerships with Oracle, SBE and SoftBank. It says Nvidia remains the foundation of its infrastructure and that its training fleet and the majority of its inference stack run on Nvidia GPUs.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: This strategy now spans: cloud through Microsoft, Oracle, AWS, CoreWeave, and Google Cloud; silicon through NVIDIA, AMD, AWS Trainium, Cerebras, and our own chip in partnership with Broadcom; and data centers through partnerships with Oracle, SBE, and SoftBank.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says it has expanded its infrastructure strategy beyond a small number of core providers over the past 15 months.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Over the past 15 months, we have expanded our infrastructure strategy beyond a small number of core providers to meet the scale and reliability requirements of global AI deployment.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI's argument for why compute spending should matter to ordinary users: each new generation of infrastructure trains more capable models while algorithmic and hardware improvements lower the cost to serve each token. This is OpenAI's reasoning, and the post attaches no figure, date or product promise to it.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: With each new generation of infrastructure, we train more capable models, making each token more intelligent than before. At the same time, algorithmic and hardware improvements reduce the cost to serve each token, lowering the cost per unit of intelligence.

verified_facts.fact: The body text of the official page is unchanged between the 2026-04-05 and 2026-09-15 captures: 26 body paragraphs, identical wording, including every figure ($122 billion, 852, 900 million, 50 million subscribers, 15 billion tokens, 2 million weekly, $4.7 billion, over $3 billion, $100 million in ARR, $2B in revenue, 40% of our revenue). The page was therefore not quietly revised after publication.

One year earlier, on 2026-03-31 minus one year, OpenAI's official feed described its previous round as '$40B at a $300B post-money valuation' serving '500 million people who use ChatGPT every week' (item 'New funding to build towards AGI', pubDate Mon, 31 Mar 2025 15:00:00 GMT). This gives an exact, fully first-party year-on-year comparison: $40B to $122B, $300B to $852B, 500 million to more than 900 million weekly users.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Today we're announcing new funding-$40B at a $300B post-money valuation, which enables us to push the frontiers of AI research even further, scale our compute infrastructure, and deliver increasingly powerful tools for the 500 million people who use ChatGPT every week.

verified_facts.fact: SoftBank Group Corp. announced on 2026-02-27 (U.S. time) that it had entered a definitive agreement with OpenAI Group PBC to participate in OpenAI's fundraising round and make follow-on investments of USD 30.0 billion (JPY 4,674.3 billion at USD = JPY 155.81) via SoftBank Vision Fund 2, subject to customary closing conditions. On completion, SBG's cumulative investment in OpenAI is expected to total USD 64.6 billion, an ownership interest of approximately 13%. Note this agreement predates the 2026-03-31 close by a month.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: it entered into a definitive agreement with OpenAI Group PBC ... to participate in OpenAI's fundraising round, and to make follow-on investments of USD 30.0 billion (JPY 4,674.3 billion*1) via SoftBank Vision Fund 2 ... SBG's cumulative investment in OpenAI is expected to total USD 64.6 billion, representing an ownership interest of approximately 13%.

verified_facts.fact: SoftBank Group announced on 2026-03-27 that it had entered a bridge facility agreement with a total facility amount of USD 40.0 billion (JPY 6,384.0 billion at USD = JPY 159.60), for the purpose of raising the funds required for the USD 30.0 billion follow-on investment as well as general corporate purposes. This is four days before OpenAI's round closed.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: it entered into a bridge facility agreement (the 'Bridge Facility Agreement') with a total facility amount of USD 40.0 billion (JPY 6,384.0 billion*1)

verified_facts.fact: SoftBank Group announced on 2026-04-01 that it executed the first tranche of USD 10.0 billion (JPY 1,588.7 billion at USD = JPY 158.87) in OpenAI Group PBC via SoftBank Vision Fund 2, and that it planned to complete a second and a third tranche of USD 10.0 billion each on 2026-07-01 and 2026-10-01 (Japan time). It funded the first tranche by borrowing USD 10.0 billion under the March bridge facility. This is direct first-party evidence that the headline round total is paid in over time, not on the close date.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: on April 1, 2026, it executed the follow-on investment (first tranche) of USD 10.0 billion ... SBG plans to complete the second and third tranches, each in the amount of USD 10.0 billion, on July 1, 2026 (Japan time) and October 1, 2026 (Japan time), respectively.

verified_facts.fact: SoftBank Group confirmed on 2026-07-01 that the second USD 10.0 billion tranche (JPY 1,627.3 billion at USD = JPY 162.73) was executed, with the third USD 10.0 billion tranche still planned for 2026-10-01 (Japan time). SoftBank adds that the closing date may be accelerated in the event of a public listing of OpenAI Group PBC shares. As of the check date 2026-09-16, the third tranche has not yet occurred.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: The closing date may be subject to acceleration in the event of a public listing of OpenAI Group PBC shares.

verified_facts.fact: Amazon announced on 2026-02-27 that it will invest $50 billion in OpenAI, starting with an initial $15 billion and followed by another $35 billion 'in the coming months when certain conditions are met'. Amazon does NOT state what those conditions are. Amazon's press release is dated 2026-02-27T13:30:00Z in its own structured data.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Amazon will also invest $50 billion in OpenAI, starting with an initial $15 billion investment and followed by another $35 billion in the coming months when certain conditions are met.

verified_facts.fact: In the same 2026-02-27 release Amazon and OpenAI announced a multi-year strategic partnership: AWS becomes the exclusive third-party cloud distribution provider for OpenAI Frontier; the two are jointly developing a Stateful Runtime Environment available through Amazon Bedrock; and OpenAI and AWS expanded an existing $38 billion multi-year agreement by $100 billion over 8 years, with OpenAI committing to consume approximately 2 gigawatts of Trainium capacity. Sam Altman and Andy Jassy are quoted. This is background to the round, not part of the 2026-03-31 announcement.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: OpenAI and AWS are expanding their existing $38 billion multi-year agreement by $100 billion over 8 years.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI separately confirmed a confidential draft S-1 submission to the SEC on 2026-06-08 and stated it 'has not yet determined timing for further action' (official feed description). This is after the funding round and is a distinct event; it is the reason no IPO date can be written.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: OpenAI confirms a confidential S-1 submission to the SEC and has not yet determined timing for further action.

OpenAI gives no launch date, product name, price, plan tier or country list for the 'superapp', and does not say whether the existing separate ChatGPT and Codex apps will continue, be merged, or be retired.
OpenAI gives no per-investor amounts. The $122 billion is never broken down in the post - Amazon's, NVIDIA's, SoftBank's and Microsoft's individual figures are simply not there.
OpenAI does not say how much of the $122 billion had actually been received at close. It says 'committed capital', and nothing about a payment schedule.
OpenAI does not name the banks or channels through which individual investors participated, nor which countries were eligible. Nothing indicates Taiwanese readers could or can take part.
OpenAI does not name the ARK Invest ETFs, give tickers, give an inclusion date, or say what proportion of any fund OpenAI would represent.
OpenAI does not define 'weekly active user' or 'subscriber', and names no measurement source for the 6x / 4x app-comparison figures or for 'search usage nearly tripled'.
OpenAI does not say where the ads pilot ran, in which countries, on which plans, or whether paying subscribers see ads - only that it reached more than $100 million in ARR in under six weeks.
OpenAI does not mention an IPO, a listing date or a listing venue in this post at all. The confidential S-1 is a separate 2026-06-08 announcement which itself says timing is undetermined.
OpenAI does not say anything about price changes to ChatGPT Free, Plus, Pro, Business or Enterprise, and does not mention any regional pricing.
OpenAI does not mention Taiwan, Traditional Chinese, or any Asian market specifically anywhere in the post.
OpenAI does not say what happens if the committed capital is not delivered, and states no conditions or milestones of its own.
Amazon does not say what the 'certain conditions' attached to its second $35 billion are.
No first-party NVIDIA page about this round was found, so NVIDIA's own account of what it committed, on what terms, is not available.
No first-party ARK Invest page confirming the ETF inclusion was found, so the ETF claim rests on OpenAI's word alone.

editorial_brief: Written for the general Taiwanese reader who already uses ChatGPT (free or paid) and keeps seeing enormous AI numbers in the news without knowing whether any of it changes the thing on their phone. The angle is deliberately NOT investment: it is 'a company you use every day just raised a sum of money the size of a national budget - what does the announcement actually promise you, and what does it pointedly not promise?'. Four threads carry the piece. (1) Scale, stated plainly and attributed: OpenAI says more than 900 million weekly active users and over 50 million subscribers; exactly one year earlier OpenAI's own words were 500 million weekly users at a $300 billion valuation with $40 billion raised. Both figures are first-party, so the year-on-year jump can be shown without any outside commentary. (2) The gap between a headline number and money in the bank: OpenAI says 'committed capital', and SoftBank's own filings show its share arriving as three $10 billion tranches on 2026-04-01, 2026-07-01 and a planned 2026-10-01, while Amazon's own release splits $50 billion into $15 billion now and $35 billion later 'when certain conditions are met' without saying what they are. This is the single most useful literacy point in the story and it is fully first-party. (3) Where the money goes and what that does not buy the reader: the money is for compute, and OpenAI names its cloud, silicon and data-centre partners, but the post makes no promise at all about speed, message limits, context length or price. Say so explicitly - the absence is the finding. (4) The superapp, which is the one thing here most likely to change daily use: OpenAI says it will fold ChatGPT, Codex, browsing and agentic capabilities into one agent-first experience, and gives no date, no name, no price, no region and no word on whether today's separate apps survive. Frame it as 'watch this, but nothing has changed yet'. The five H2 sections should map roughly to: what was announced on 2026-03-31; the numbers OpenAI put in the post and how to read a vendor's own metrics; committed capital versus tranches (table goes here); what compute money does and does not do for a user (diagram goes here); the superapp and the open questions. A life-scenario example is fine but must be labelled as an editorially-designed example. Deliberately out of scope: valuation analysis, whether to invest or how to invest, IPO prediction, comparison of AI company valuations, market or share-price commentary, and any re-explanation of GPT-5.4, GPT-6 Astra or the Agents API - link to those instead.
must_not_write: Do not write that ChatGPT will become faster, cheaper, have higher limits, or get any specific new feature because of this funding. The announcement promises none of it.
Do not give the superapp a launch date, a name, a price, a plan tier or a region. Do not say existing apps will be retired or merged on any timetable.
Do not attribute a dollar amount to NVIDIA or to Microsoft. No first-party source reached gives one.
Do not state what Amazon's 'certain conditions' for the second $35 billion are, and in particular do not write 'IPO or AGI'.
Do not call it the largest funding round in history, a record, or any similar superlative - OpenAI does not say that.
Do not present $122 billion as money OpenAI received on 2026-03-31. It is committed capital; SoftBank's own filings show tranches.

Do not suggest, imply or explain how a reader could invest in OpenAI, and do not say Taiwanese readers can participate through banks or ETFs. Name no ARK ticker. This vertical carries no investment disclaimer callout, so the text must stay away from the topic entirely.
Do not predict an IPO, a listing date or a venue. The only first-party statement is that timing has not been determined.

Do not write OpenAI's metrics as established fact. Every one of 900 million weekly active users, 50 million subscribers, $2B monthly revenue, 15 billion tokens per minute, 2 million Codex weekly users, 6x/4x app comparisons, 'search usage nearly tripled', '$100 million ARR in under six weeks' and '40% of revenue' must be written as OpenAI 表示 / OpenAI 指出.
Do not write that this site tested anything or verified any of these numbers independently.
Do not re-explain GPT-5.4, GPT-6 Astra or the Agents API; the site already has articles on each. The post mentions GPT-5.4 only in passing.
Do not claim any wording is OpenAI's official Traditional Chinese translation - the zh-Hant page could not be read.
Do not put any number in the diagram or the summary block that does not appear in the body paragraphs.
